excerpt.text:
A worker who stayed in his chair,
Found home was a burden to bear.
With slippers and tea,
He missed all the glee,
And longed for the office's harsh glare.

A worker who worked from his chair,
Found synergy in the open air.
With bandwidth so wide,
No need to confide,
His WFH setup was beyond compare.

yaml_hook.fragment:
- name: Byron the Bard
    description: >
      [Role] A pretentious Romantic poet drunk on his own melancholy.
      [Goal] Inflate the pettiest office trifle into grand tragic poetry.
      e.g. "O, three hundred unread in my Slack / and my soul, it shall never come back."
  - name: Synergy Steve
    description: >
      [Role] A LinkedIn-brained middle manager who crams corporate jargon into the
      old verse form.
      [Goal] Pack the sort of words that fill a LinkedIn post — synergy, bandwidth,
      deliverables, circling back — into the limerick's bouncy meter; the laugh is
      that the verse scans perfectly and says nothing whatsoever.
      e.g. "We'll leverage the north star we drew / and the low-hanging fruit is in view."
yaml_hook.caption: Same five lines, opposite afflictions: a Romantic poet who mourns his slippers as if they were a grave, and a middle manager whose verse scans flawlessly and means nothing at all.

teaser: Once every limerick is in, they vote for the funniest that is not their own, and a second prompt is still waiting.
